title: The 2026 M&A Report: Regional Perspectives
gist: BCG's 2026 regional M&A survey finds a global recovery driven almost entirely by a shrinking number of megadeals -- value up, volume down in nearly every region -- with European dealmaker sentiment (100) running well ahead of the Americas (73), sharp divergence across Asia-Pacific sub-markets, and AI showing up both as a deal driver (SpaceX/Anysphere, data-center power M&A) and as a structural theme (China's 'dual AI agenda').

themes.theme: Global Cross-Currents: Megadeal Concentration and Sentiment Gap

insights.claim: BCG's global M&A Sentiment Index, which tracks dealmakers' willingness to transact roughly six months ahead, rose to 83 in 2026 from 79 at the start of the year but remains below its long-term average of 100, indicating a real but incomplete recovery.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Use the sentiment index as a leading indicator of deal conditions roughly six months out; a reading still below 100 signals the recovery has further to run before broad-based activity returns.
insights.quote: Globally, BCG’s M&A Sentiment Index, which tracks dealmakers’ willingness to transact approximately six months ahead, stands at 83, up from 79 at the beginning of the year but still below its long-term average of 100.
insights.locator: Globally, BCG's M&A Sentiment Index

insights.claim: Across nearly every region covered, the 2026 M&A recovery is defined by a shrinking number of very large transactions driving up aggregate deal value even as overall deal volume declines, a barbell pattern that recurs from Africa to the US to Germany.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Investors should expect concentrated upside in large-cap consolidation and take-private plays rather than a broad rebound in smaller-deal activity; screen for megadeal-adjacent names rather than the broader M&A tape.
insights.locator: The global M&A market has returned to growth

insights.claim: European dealmaker sentiment matched its long-term average at 100 in 2026, running markedly ahead of the Americas at 73 and the global benchmark of 83, reflecting the continent's comparative stability amid an uncertain global environment.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A confidence gap this wide favors European completion rates over US/Americas deals near-term; watch for European M&A-linked equities and merger-arb spreads to reflect the stronger conviction.
insights.quote: the region has matched its long-term average, markedly ahead of the Americas at 73
insights.locator: Regionally, BCG's M&A Sentiment Index shows strong confidence among European dealmakers

themes.theme: Africa: Gulf Capital Moves In as Local Acquirers Retreat

insights.claim: Africa-linked deal value rose 19% to $11.6 billion through July 2026 even as deal volume fell 32% (from 294 to 200 transactions), showing that value growth was concentrated rather than broad-based, consistent with the global pattern.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Headline Africa M&A growth overstates market depth; investors targeting African deal flow should expect a thin, concentrated opportunity set rather than a broadening market.
insights.locator: Africa's M&A market found firmer footing

insights.claim: Just three Africa-linked deals worth $500 million or more (versus nine in each of the prior two years) accounted for roughly 75% of total 2026 Africa deal value at $8.7 billion, with average megadeal size more than doubling to $2.9 billion from $1.1 billion, while the other ~197 smaller deals totaled only about $2.9 billion combined.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Africa's M&A story in 2026 is really a story of three transactions; diversified exposure to African M&A remains unattractive versus targeting the specific megadeals directly.
insights.locator: Only three transactions worth $500 million or more

insights.claim: Africa's inbound/outbound M&A pattern reversed in 2026: deal value targeting African companies rose 63% to $7.8 billion while deal value involving African acquirers buying abroad fell 44% to $4.7 billion, the opposite of the weaker-inbound, resilient-outbound pattern seen in 2025.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Foreign strategic and financial buyers are moving decisively on African assets while local capital pulls back from overseas deals -- a window for foreign acquirers to buy African assets while local competition for those same assets is receding.
insights.locator: The rebound is also uneven between inbound and outbound activity

insights.claim: South32's agreement to sell five aluminum value-chain assets (Worsley Alumina, Hillside Aluminium, the MRN bauxite mine, and its Brazilian alumina and aluminum operations) to Alcoa for an estimated $5.5 billion is a rare instance of a major diversified miner divesting an entire commodity value chain to a US strategic buyer.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Signals a broader portfolio-simplification trend among diversified miners and Alcoa's consolidation of the global aluminum value chain -- relevant for materials-sector positioning and M&A-driven commodity supply-chain plays.
insights.quote: The transaction represents a rare instance of a major diversified miner divesting an entire commodity value chain to a US strategic buyer.
insights.locator: Materials and Mining

insights.claim: Private-equity-linked deal value in Africa nearly tripled to $2.9 billion from $1.0 billion even as PE deal count fell from 58 to 46, lifting PE's share of total Africa-linked deal value from about one-tenth to roughly one-quarter, though the broader re-engagement of global PE seen in 2024-2025 has slowed markedly in 2026.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Africa-focused PE capital is consolidating into fewer, larger deals (e.g., real estate via Vukile Property Fund) rather than broadening its footprint -- a signal to watch for follow-on concentration in specific sectors like real estate.
insights.locator: Deal value linked to private equity (PE) nearly tripled

themes.theme: Western Europe: France, Germany, and Italy Diverge on Value vs. Volume

insights.claim: The proposed roughly $24 billion breakup and acquisition of SFR by a consortium of Bouygues Telecom, Free (Iliad's subsidiary), and Orange is one of Europe's largest announced 2026 transactions and would reshape the French telecom market, underscoring how deals touching critical infrastructure hinge on regulatory execution.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Watch regulatory clearance timelines closely -- the deal's completion risk is explicitly framed as the swing factor for whether France's telecom consolidation actually plays out.
insights.quote: The proposed acquisition and break-up of SFR by a consortium comprising Bouygues Telecom, Free (a subsidiary of Iliad), and Orange would reshape the French telecommunications market.
insights.locator: Telecommunications was the defining sector for French M&A

insights.claim: Publicis Groupe's acquisition of LiveRamp is framed as emblematic of French companies increasingly using M&A specifically to accelerate AI-enabled business models and data-driven marketing capabilities rather than pursuing scale alone.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI-capability acquisition is becoming a distinct, separately trackable rationale in European dealmaking beyond traditional scale or cost-synergy logic.
insights.locator: Technology, Media, and Marketing Services

insights.claim: French health-care deal activity slowed in the first seven months of 2026 versus the same period in 2025 (which was marked by Sanofi's landmark Opella transaction), yet French pharma companies kept buying abroad, with Servier acquiring Edgewise Therapeutics and Day One Biopharmaceuticals to strengthen its innovation pipeline.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Pipeline-acquisition demand from French pharma persists independent of headline sector volume -- a durable source of cross-border biotech deal flow even in a slower year.
insights.locator: Health Care and Life Sciences

insights.claim: Germany was one of the few major 2026 M&A markets to post gains in both deal value (+122% year over year, 45% above the ten-year average) and deal volume (+4%), sharply diverging from global (+19% value / -16% volume) and European (+57% value / -14% volume) trends.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Germany stands out as the one major market where M&A breadth, not just headline value, is genuinely recovering -- a differentiated allocation case versus other developed markets stuck in the value-up/volume-down pattern.
insights.quote: Germany was one of the few major markets to record increases in both deal value and deal volume.
insights.locator: Aggregate deal value surged, propelled by a handful of very large transactions

insights.claim: Germany's largest 2026 deals were concentrated in industrials and materials -- Kone's roughly $23.7 billion acquisition of TK Elevator, Lone Star's approximately $4.9 billion purchase of Continental's ContiTech unit, and Henkel's roughly $2.5 billion acquisition of Stahl -- with private equity accounting for about two-thirds of German deal value and 37% of deal volume across 21 large deals ($500 million-plus), including three megadeals ($10 billion-plus).
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: PE dry powder is a dominant driver of Germany's recovery; German industrials/materials carve-outs are a concentrated hunting ground for sponsor-backed deal flow.
insights.locator: Industrials and Materials

insights.claim: Germany's IPO market is reviving alongside M&A: first-half 2026 listings raised roughly €750 million, approximately double both the number and value of listings from a year earlier, reinforced by a broader revival in US listings.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A recovering German IPO market alongside strong M&A suggests PE sponsors have multiple viable exit routes reopening simultaneously, which could accelerate further deal-making as portfolios turn over.
insights.locator: Germany's IPO market extended its tentative recovery

insights.claim: Italy diverged sharply from the rest of Europe in 2026, posting its highest deal volume in a decade (more than 900 deals, ~20% above the ten-year average) while aggregate deal value fell 26% to $39.9 billion -- breadth rather than scale defined the market, structurally explained by Italy's long tail of family-owned small and mid-cap businesses reaching succession points.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Italy is the one major European market where deal-count breadth, not megadeal concentration, is the investable signal -- favors exposure to succession-driven midmarket deal flow and advisory/financing activity over headline large-cap plays.
insights.quote: While Europe and the global market concentrated activity in fewer and larger transactions, Italy recorded broad-based dealmaking by volume but with lower aggregate value.
insights.locator: Italy's M&A market stood apart

insights.claim: Poste Italiane's $12.5 billion acquisition of Telecom Italia, announced in March 2026, returns Italy's largest telecom operator to significant state control nearly three decades after its privatization.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A notable case of re-nationalization via M&A in a major European telecom market -- worth tracking as a possible template for state re-engagement elsewhere in strategic infrastructure sectors.
insights.locator: Telecommunications. Poste Italiane's $12.5 billion acquisition

insights.claim: The $12.1 billion take-private of Milan-listed Recordati by a CVC Capital Partners/Groupe Bruxelles Lambert consortium backed by ADIA, CPPIB, and PSP is one of Europe's largest health-care buyouts in recent years, and overseas bidders participated in nine of the ten largest Italian sponsor deals in the first seven months of 2026.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Italian PE deal flow is now dominated by international capital rather than domestic sponsors -- global institutional investors seeking Italian assets should note sovereign wealth and pension co-investment is already the norm, not the exception.
insights.locator: The third-largest deal in Italy so far this year

insights.claim: Italy's reformed Consolidated Law on Finance, in force since late April 2026, lowers takeover execution risk via a uniform 30% mandatory bid threshold, a 90% squeeze-out threshold, and a new shareholder-approved cash acquisition route, while separately Law 4/2026 expands the Golden Power foreign-investment screening regime with an economic and financial security test.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Italy is simultaneously easing domestic takeover mechanics and tightening foreign-investment screening -- foreign acquirers of Italian strategic assets should expect faster public-deal execution but more scrutiny at the entry point.
insights.quote: a uniform 30% mandatory bid threshold, a 90% squeeze-out threshold, and a new shareholder-approved cash acquisition route
insights.locator: Italy's 2026 regulatory reforms

themes.theme: Middle East: Sovereign Capital Repositions After a Peak Year

insights.claim: Middle East M&A pulled back sharply in 2026 (deal value -25%, volume -8%) even as global deal value rose 19%, following an exceptional 2025 in which sovereign funds and state-linked companies deployed capital heavily to advance industrial policy and Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 diversification program.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The region is entering a more selective capital-deployment phase after an exceptional prior year -- expect fewer but more targeted sovereign-backed transactions rather than a broad slowdown in Gulf dealmaking capacity.
insights.locator: M&A activity in the Middle East declined

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, through its Savvy Games Group, acquired ByteDance's Shanghai-based Moonton Technology (maker of Mobile Legends) for $6.0 billion, extending a deliberate multiyear gaming and esports consolidation strategy that also includes ESL FACEIT ($1.5 billion, 2022), Scopely ($4.9 billion, 2023), and Niantic's games business ($3.5 billion, 2025), alongside a pending $55 billion PIF-led take-private of Electronic Arts.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: PIF is building a globally dominant gaming/esports portfolio piece by piece; the pending $55 billion Electronic Arts take-private would be a landmark test of sovereign-fund control over a major listed US gaming publisher -- watch regulatory response closely.
insights.quote: Together, the transactions point to a deliberate strategy to consolidate a leading global position in gaming and esports.
insights.locator: Technology, Media, and Telecommunications

insights.claim: The Middle East has become an increasingly important exit market for global financial sponsors and corporates in 2026 -- American Industrial Partners, Macquarie, ByteDance, Shell, SLB, and The Energy & Minerals Group all sold assets to regional sovereign funds or state-linked companies, underscoring Gulf buyers' growing influence and ability to shape terms and valuations in competitive sales processes.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Global sponsors seeking exits should treat Gulf sovereign funds as a primary, price-setting bidder class rather than a secondary buyer -- their growing leverage in auctions can compress achievable premiums for other bidders.
insights.locator: The region became an increasingly important exit market

insights.claim: Abu Dhabi consolidated ADQ into L'IMAD Holding Company in 2026, creating a sovereign investment platform that manages roughly $300 billion in assets with a mandate to deploy capital both domestically and internationally.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A newly consolidated $300 billion sovereign platform with an explicit international deployment mandate is a significant new global buyer to track across sectors going forward.
insights.locator: a significant restructuring of Abu Dhabi's sovereign investment landscape

themes.theme: Nordics: A Rebound Riding on One Megadeal

insights.claim: Nordic deal value surged roughly 74% year over year through July 2026 (versus +19% globally and +57% in Europe) almost entirely because of a single transaction, the Kone-TK Elevator combination, while Nordic deal volume fell about 6% -- a value-led rebound rather than a broad-based recovery.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Strip out the single Kone-TK Elevator megadeal and Nordic M&A momentum looks far weaker -- investors should not extrapolate the headline Nordic growth rate to the broader regional deal market.
insights.locator: Aggregate deal value surged, but the increase was driven almost entirely by a single megadeal

insights.claim: Kone's approximately $23.7 billion combination with German elevator maker TK Elevator is the largest deal in Finnish corporate history and one of the largest private-equity exits ever in Europe.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A landmark PE exit of this scale signals sponsors are willing to crystallize large European industrial holdings when strategic buyer demand is strong -- watch for similar-sized PE-to-strategic exits elsewhere in European industrials.
insights.quote: the largest deal in Finnish corporate history and one of the largest private equity exits ever in Europe
insights.locator: Industrials and Machinery

insights.claim: Financial sponsors were involved in approximately 75% of Nordic deal value and roughly a third of deal volume in 2026, with country-level conditions diverging: Sweden remains the PE center with resilient tech/industrials but leveraged real estate under pressure, Norway sees modest cross-border activity amid higher-for-longer rates, Denmark benefits from life sciences and renewables, and Finland continues outbound industrial dealmaking for scale.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Nordic M&A exposure needs a country-specific lens rather than a regional blanket view -- Sweden for PE/tech-industrial resilience, Denmark for life-sciences consolidation, Finland for outbound industrial scale plays.
insights.locator: Conditions will vary meaningfully by country

themes.theme: UK: Larger but Fewer Deals, With Two-Thirds of Value Still Pending

insights.claim: UK M&A deal value nearly doubled to $235.3 billion from $119.0 billion year over year even as deal volume fell to 1,763 transactions from 2,272 -- a year of "larger but fewer deals" -- and the UK's share of total European deal value rose to 37% from 29%.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The UK is capturing a growing share of European deal value even as breadth narrows -- large-cap UK targets are becoming disproportionately important to overall European M&A flow.
insights.quote: For the UK M&A market, 2026 has so far been a year of larger but fewer deals.
insights.locator: For the UK M&A market, 2026 has so far been a year of larger but fewer deals

insights.claim: Just 65 UK transactions worth more than $500 million generated 88% of total 2026 UK deal value, with average large-deal size rising from $1.6 billion to $3.2 billion, while foreign inbound acquisitions of UK assets returned to levels comparable to the 2021-2022 cycle.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: UK M&A value is now overwhelmingly a large-cap, foreign-inbound story -- a return of overseas buyers to UK-listed targets at a scale not seen since the 2021-2022 boom is a key signal for UK equity risk-arb positioning.
insights.locator: One notable feature of the market was the return of foreign acquirers

insights.claim: McCormick's proposed $44.8 billion acquisition of Unilever's food business is so large it alone exceeds the rest of the UK consumer sector's announced 2026 deal value combined, while Eli Lilly's $7.9 billion acquisition of Centessa Pharmaceuticals drove most of the increase in UK health-care deal value.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sector-level UK deal value figures are being distorted by single blockbuster transactions -- strip out McCormick/Unilever and Eli Lilly/Centessa to see the true underlying trend in UK consumer and health-care M&A.
insights.locator: Consumer Goods and Health Care

insights.claim: UK financial institutions and real estate deal value more than doubled to $67.4 billion, led by Nuveen's proposed $12.9 billion acquisition of Schroders, Zurich's $10.9 billion acquisition of insurer Beazley, and Prologis's roughly $18.7 billion takeover of Segro -- the UK's most broadly distributed sectoral increase in deal value in 2026.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Unlike the concentrated consumer/health-care gains, financial institutions/real estate strength is spread across multiple large deals, making it the most durable source of UK deal momentum per the article.
insights.locator: Financial Institutions and Real Estate

insights.claim: UK private-equity sponsor deal value rose 49% to $105.8 billion, and EQT's $12.6 billion offer for Intertek would be the largest UK public-to-private transaction in nearly two decades, but three large sponsor-led take-private attempts were withdrawn during the year, highlighting continuing execution risk in acquiring UK-listed companies.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sponsor appetite for UK public-to-private deals is strong but execution risk is real -- roughly two-thirds of the year's announced UK deal value (including Unilever, Schroders, Beazley, and Intertek) remains pending, so completion risk is the key variable to watch through year-end.
insights.locator: EQT's $12.6 billion offer for Intertek would be the largest UK public-to-private transaction

themes.theme: US: A Bifurcated Market Where AI Is Reshaping Deal Logic

insights.claim: US M&A shows a widening bifurcation in 2026: deal value rose 25% (versus +19% globally) while deal volume fell 26% (versus -16% globally), with overall transaction activity dropping to its lowest level since the pandemic-disrupted first half of 2020, even as activity above $500 million reached its highest level in three years.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Broad US deal volume is at a multi-year low even as headline value looks strong -- an investor relying on volume-based M&A indicators for the US would be badly misled; focus on the large-cap tape instead.
insights.locator: A widening gap between deal value and deal volume has defined US M&A activity

insights.claim: The bidding war between Netflix and Paramount Skydance for Warner Bros. Discovery, which ultimately valued the company at roughly $80 billion, and Fox Corporation's proposed $25 billion acquisition of Roku both underscore the strategic value US media companies now place on premium content and scaled streaming distribution.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Media consolidation is intensifying around distribution scale and content control -- competitive bidding at this size suggests further consolidation pressure on remaining independent streaming/media assets.
insights.locator: Technology, Media, and Telecommunications

insights.claim: SpaceX's $60 billion acquisition of Anysphere, developer of the Cursor AI coding platform, illustrates how intensely companies -- including ones outside traditional software -- are competing to secure leading AI software capabilities.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: AI-capability acquisition is spreading well beyond pure tech/software buyers into capital-rich adjacent industrials -- expect more cross-industry buyers to bid aggressively for AI coding/software startups regardless of sector fit.
insights.locator: SpaceX's $60 billion acquisition of Anysphere

insights.claim: NextEra's $67 billion acquisition of Dominion Energy reflects growing competition to secure power generation and grid capacity amid rising electricity demand from data centers, making it one of the clearest examples of AI infrastructure buildout directly driving utility M&A.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Data-center power demand is now a direct, quantifiable driver of utility M&A premiums -- a key thesis link for investors positioning in power-generation and grid-capacity assets tied to the AI buildout.
insights.quote: reflected growing competition to secure generation and grid capacity amid the rising demands of data centers for electricity
insights.locator: In power and utilities, NextEra's $67 billion acquisition of Dominion Energy

insights.claim: US health care remained an "always-on" M&A sector, accounting for roughly one-fifth of total US deal value, with biopharma buyers targeting differentiated pipelines (AbbVie's $11 billion acquisition of Apogee, Vertex Pharmaceuticals' $10 billion acquisition of Crinetics) and medtech consolidating around product and clinical capability (Boston Scientific's $15 billion acquisition of Penumbra, Danaher's $14 billion acquisition of Masimo).
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Health care remains the most reliable, cycle-resistant US M&A sector -- a defensive allocation within an otherwise bifurcated deal market, with biopharma pipeline scarcity and medtech scale both sustaining premium valuations.
insights.locator: Health Care. Health care again proved to be an always-on sector

insights.claim: Asia-Pacific M&A declined overall in 2026 (volume -9%, value -14%), but this masks sharp divergence beneath the surface: Southeast Asia, India, and Japan showed bright spots while Australia/New Zealand hit decade lows and Greater China's headline decline conceals an improving structural picture.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Treat Asia-Pacific as a set of distinct micro-markets rather than a single regional trade -- headline regional figures mask meaningfully different investable dynamics by country.
insights.locator: Dealmaking in Asia-Pacific was down over the first seven months of 2026

insights.claim: Australia and New Zealand M&A hit its lowest completed-deal-value level in a decade in fiscal year 2026 (down one-third year over year), driven by four combined forces: new regulations extending approval timelines, the growing influence of superannuation funds, global instability, and persistent buyer-seller valuation gaps, with inbound deals falling to their lowest level since 2017.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The Australian M&A slump is structural (regulation, superannuation-fund influence) as much as cyclical -- don't expect a quick rebound absent regulatory or valuation-gap resolution; Australia's energy-transition supplier role remains the one bright spot attracting investors.
insights.locator: Australia and New Zealand

insights.claim: Greater China's M&A market is transitioning from a broad, market-wide investment opportunity to a collection of "investable micromarkets," marked by financial sponsors seeking control structures for alpha generation, Mainland China becoming a magnet for exportable IP, a "dual AI agenda" of consolidating strategically important AI assets alongside separate investment in Mainland China's own AI stack architecture, and outbound deals becoming more targeted at closing specific strategic gaps rather than trophy-driven.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: China's declining headline deal figures are misleading -- the underlying shift toward control-oriented PE structures and a bifurcated AI investment stack (domestic vs. globally aligned) is the more important structural signal for investors positioning in Chinese tech and AI assets.
insights.quote: Greater China is transitioning from a broad, market-wide investment opportunity to a collection of investable micromarkets.
insights.locator: Greater China

insights.claim: India's declining deal count (-20%) alongside near-stable deal value (-2%) suggests dealmakers are exercising discipline rather than losing appetite: deals over $1 billion rose 14 percentage points as a share of activity, transactions above $500 million have accounted for 59% of total Indian deal value since 2024, and outbound deal value rose $3.8 billion even as domestic and inbound value both declined.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Indian dealmakers are selectively pursuing bigger, higher-conviction bets while waiting on policy clarity -- and Indian outbound acquirers are becoming a growing source of overseas deal flow even as domestic and inbound activity softens.
insights.locator: India

insights.claim: Japan's M&A deal volume grew 2.8% in 2026, propelled partly by a regulatory shift that has normalized proactive, unsolicited acquisition proposals for listed companies as a standard strategic tool, forcing listed companies to preemptively articulate and execute their own full-potential plans or face pressure to respond to bids.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Rising proactive/unsolicited-bid activity in Japan is a structural regulatory shift, not a cyclical blip -- likely to sustain elevated Japanese M&A and shareholder-pressure-driven corporate restructuring for years, a durable theme for Japan-focused activist and event-driven strategies.
insights.locator: Japan

insights.claim: South Korea's M&A market is concentrating sharply at the top -- the country's ten largest transactions accounted for 44% of 2025 deal value, up from 28% in 2022 -- while corporate divestitures, not new acquisitions, are the market's "hidden engine," accounting for nearly 48% of deal count and more than 60% of deal value from 2021 to 2025.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Divestiture-driven deal flow, not new M&A, is the primary route for ownership reallocation in South Korea -- investors tracking Korean corporate restructuring should focus on carve-out and divestiture activity as the core signal, not headline acquisition counts.
insights.quote: the hidden engine behind a significant share of deals and deal value in the country is corporate divestiture, which serves as the market’s primary route for reallocating ownership.
insights.locator: South Korea
